hypothesis: Sample-varying coordinate signs improve classification beyond source-fixed coordinate orientation after equal-budget adaptation.
alternative: T02 signed advantage is reproducible by a fixed source-derived sign orientation and does not require per-sample signs.
template: s0=sign(mean source u), sign(0)=+1; choose 256 distinct FF++ training videos by sorted SHA256(n01-t03-template-v1:+raw image path), first encountered image per video; fixed preprocessing RNG3407, initial pretrained encoder, no gradients; save full indices/image hashes/template. No target input or tuning. Same buffer in both arms.
controls: unit norm and per-coordinate magnitude formula
evaluation: same 192 development videos, one frame/video, 64/domain; no independent final-test claim
criterion: deltaCE=CE_template-CE_signed >=0.02nat and deltaAUC=AUC_signed-AUC_template >=0.01 and every domain deltaCE>=0 supports sample-specific sign; either macro delta<=0 not supported, otherwise inconclusive. No equivalence conclusion.
dedup: T02 signed/abs cannot distinguish sample-specific information from fixed orientation; D02 sign-only donor response J=0.0000679583 did not support label-conditioned sensitivity. Neither prior nor 4090 N05 has a fixed source template training arm. Signed is a paired bridge control, not seed exploration.
limits: template estimated at initial encoder and frozen while LoRA adapts
template may omit rare coordinate structures
abs and fixed template retain same information and differ in orientation/optimization
null is not equivalence or absence of sign information
